_about: frontier reference points, for reading the open-weights roster against.
SOURCE, not derived: which model is worth comparing to is a judgement, and
this file holds only that judgement plus the reason. every NUMBER comes from
data/artificial-analysis.json at build time, joined on `slug`.
nothing here is a roster member and nothing here can become one. the whole
claim of this registry is `best of what i can run`, and every percentile on
the page is computed within the open-weights cohort -- README's `the cohort
is this registry` says why. a milestone is a LINE DRAWN OVER that cohort. if
one ever enters the cohort it silently moves every percentile and every
quality score on the page, so `isOpenWeights` being false is checked rather
than assumed.
the numbers are joined live rather than frozen, which is deliberate and is a
trade. artificial analysis restates scores as it re-runs models, so a frozen
milestone would drift away from the roster it is drawn against and the
comparison would quietly stop being like-for-like. the cost is that this
file's meaning depends on a capture that moves; the benefit is that both
sides of the comparison move together.
`reasoning` is picked from the data, not from taste: 41 of the 44 registry
models artificial analysis scores map to an `isReasoning: true` slug, so the
reasoning arm is the like-for-like one. the three that do not are coder
models with no reasoning mode at all.

claude-opus-4-5-thinking.label: Claude Opus 4.5
why: the leading model on the intelligence index on the day it shipped, and the
reference point for `what did the frontier look like before the open
weights caught up`. on that date the best open-weights model artificial
analysis scored was Kimi K2 Thinking, 8.4 index points behind it.
